title: How Tibo shipped 11 products in 4 months, found Tweet Hunter, and grew it 7x to a multi-million exit
summary: Tibo recounts two failed startups, then a "fail in two weeks, not two years" approach: ship a product a week and judge only by revenue. That led to Tweet Hunter (the 11th product), built on his own problem and grown through building in public, SEO and an influencer partner, then sold on a 20% upfront / 80% milestone deal. He also covers owning your audience via newsletters, AI shifting value to distribution, and partnering with makers instead of hiring.

principles.text: Fail fast: ship a new product every week and judge it by revenue alone, not vanity metrics.
principles.quote: if we need to fail again it it needs to be in two weeks and not in two years and so we started this process of trying to ship a new product every week or so until something actually sticken until we get Revenue

principles.text: Build for your own problems; you only deeply understand the core need of problems you live yourself.
principles.quote: I would really start building something for yourself first because you are an expert on your own problems like building a good product is in the first place a true understanding of the problem that you are solving

principles.text: Free users without paying conversion are not a real business; revenue is the signal.
principles.quote: if people do not convert to paid user you don't have a real product like you don't have a real business

principles.text: Building in public earns trust, which brings feedback, sales and promotion. Sharing tips gets you the credit.
principles.quote: if you are the guy sharing the tips you get something what that that is amazing today which is trust and by by doing that by sharing value every day on Twitter by just sharing tips by showing true numbers what happens is people start trusting you

principles.text: Don't rely on social platforms alone: you don't own followers. Own a newsletter list, and keep exportable backups.
principles.quote: you do not own your followers you do not own your um like your accounts it can just get suspended at any time what you truly own is a newsletter subscriber base

principles.text: As AI drives build costs toward zero, value shifts to distribution, storytelling and educating users.
principles.quote: building cost are slowly going to zero ... the value will be in distribution in your capability to distribute an existing product and to create a nice story telling about it and to educate people on how to use product properly
